cards.title: Turn on GitHub Issues for void-model
cards.plain: GitHub turns Issues off on forks, so this repo has no tracker for bugs and security items. The global rule wants Git Issues.
cards.why: Every bug and security finding should have an issue that the fixing commit closes. The agent's GitHub App token cannot change repository settings.
steps: Open https://github.com/chappa-ai-llc/void-model/settings on your phone or desktop.
While there, open **Settings › Code security** (https://github.com/chappa-ai-llc/void-model/settings/security_analysis) and check that **Dependabot alerts** is on.
cards.verify: https://github.com/chappa-ai-llc/void-model/issues opens instead of returning to the code page.
cards.blocks: Filing the decord and Kubric follow-ups as issues (they are timeline rows until then).

cards.title: Security sweep: patched dependencies, unsafe loading fixed, dead web API removed
cards.plain: All 82 open advisories (5 critical, 43 high) are fixed by upgrading 7 packages, and the code no longer loads untrusted pickles or checkpoints unsafely.
cards.chosen: Pillow 13.0.0, torch 2.14.1 / torchvision 0.29.1, transformers 5.21.1, diffusers 0.42.1, accelerate 1.15.0, datasets 5.1.0, requests 2.34.2 (each release at least two weeks old, 0 OSV advisories across all 144 resolved packages). `torch.load` always uses `weights_only=True`; pickles go through a restricted loader; `trust_remote_code` removed. The unauthenticated FastAPI/Gradio code in `videox_fun/api` and `videox_fun/ui` was deleted: it was not importable (missing `controller` module), and it let any caller load any model path, fetch any URL and read any file. The notebook now clones this repo instead of upstream's vulnerable pins. Details: `docs/SECURITY.md`.
cards.why: Security rows are due 2 days (critical) and 7 days (high) from first sight (SPEC §6.1). Removing broken, unreachable network code is safer than hardening it.
cards.if_ignored: Nothing to do: confirm, or overturn if you want a demo UI back (it would be rebuilt with a login and the self-check page).

about.what: An offline, ARM64-ready edition of Netflix's VOID model: removes objects from videos together with the physical effects they cause (shadows, falls, collisions), built on CogVideoX.
about.why: The upstream VOID release depends on cloud APIs and x86 binaries. This edition runs fully offline on DGX Spark (ARM64, Ubuntu 24.04), with a local Gemma model for mask reasoning and a prebuilt decord wheel, so video inpainting can run without sending footage to a third party.
about.who: chappa.ai and researchers who run video object removal and its training or synthetic-data pipelines on their own GPU hosts, especially DGX Spark.
